sources.origin: Reuters report on T-Mobile Q2 2026 outlook

claims.claim: T-Mobile links licensed spectrum and dense radio/network infrastructure to the human need for ubiquitous connectivity; in a mature wireless market the bottleneck shifts from subscriber access toward spectrum efficiency, network quality, retention and monetization.

Strong free-cash-flow capacity improves resilience and funds network/adjacency investment, but fiber and broadband expansion create successor capital-allocation and integration bottlenecks rather than eliminating wireless saturation.

causalEdges.mechanism: mobile data requires scarce spectrum plus physical network investment
T-Mobile operates nationwide wireless infrastructure and monetizes network access
growth increasingly depends on retention, premium monetization and adjacencies rather than first-time subscriber capture

contradictions: Mature cash generation strengthens resilience while simultaneously indicating that future growth depends more on monetization and adjacencies than subscriber land-grab.
unknowns: durability of premium-plan migration without churn deterioration
falsifiers: persistent churn/net-add deterioration after pricing changes
fiber/adjacency returns failing to cover incremental capital and integration costs

recommendation.reason: Structural chain is complete; underwriting of returns and valuation remains Alpha-owned.
